title: Theory of Forms
summary: Non-physical, timeless, perfect archetypes or essences (e.g., Justice, Beauty, Circle) represent the highest and most fundamental reality, of which material objects are imperfect copies.

title: Teleology & The Four Causes
summary: Everything in nature is understood through four causes: material, formal, efficient, and final (telos - purpose or intrinsic end toward which it aims).

title: Eudaimonia & The Golden Mean
summary: Human flourishing achieved through habitual cultivation of virtues, which lie as a balanced mean between two extremes of excess and deficiency.

title: Ataraxia (Tranquility of Mind)
summary: A state of serene mental calmness free from fear, anxiety, and vain desires, considered the highest ethical state in Hellenistic philosophy.

title: Dichotomy of Control
summary: The foundational Stoic distinction between things in our power (beliefs, desires, impulses) and things outside our power (health, wealth, reputation).

title: Sunyata (Emptiness & Dependent Arising)
summary: All things are devoid of independent, self-contained essence (svabhava); entities exist solely in relational interdependence.

title: The Floating Man Thought Experiment
summary: If a person were created fully adult floating in a sensory void, they would still possess direct self-awareness of their soul without bodily sensory input.

title: Ockham's Razor (Principle of Parsimony)
summary: Plurality should not be posited without necessity; when presented with competing hypotheses, the one that makes the fewest assumptions is preferred.

title: Methodological Doubt & Cogito
summary: Radical doubt dismantles all sensory knowledge, leaving the indubitable truth: I think, therefore I exist (the thinking ego as foundation of knowledge).

title: Substance Dualism (Mind vs. Matter)
summary: Reality consists of two fundamentally distinct substances: thinking, non-extended substance (res cogitans) and physical extended substance (res extensa).

title: Pantheism (Deus Sive Natura)
summary: There is only one infinite substance, of which both mind and matter are infinite attributes: God and Nature are identical.

title: Tabula Rasa (The Blank Slate)
summary: The mind is born without innate ideas; all conceptual content and knowledge are derived entirely from experience (sensation and reflection).

title: The Problem of Induction & Hume's Fork
summary: Past observations cannot logically guarantee future occurrences without assuming nature's uniformity, a circular premise reason cannot prove.

title: Bundle Theory of the Self
summary: When we look inward, we perceive only fleeting perceptions, sensations, and emotions—there is no fixed, permanent underlying self.

title: The General Will & The Social Contract
summary: Legitimate collective political authority expresses the common interest of citizens seeking the public good, rather than the sum of private interests.

title: Transcendental Idealism (Copernican Turn)
summary: Instead of our knowledge conforming to objects, objects of experience must conform to the synthetic a priori conditions of human cognition (Space, Time, Categories).

title: Phenomena vs. Noumena (Thing-in-Itself)
summary: We can only know reality as it appears to our sensory faculties (phenomena); the thing-in-itself (noumenon) is permanently inaccessible to theoretical reason.

title: The Categorical Imperative
summary: Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law; treat humanity always as an end, never merely as a means.

title: Dialectical Historical Reason
summary: Concepts and historical institutions develop through internal tensions and contradictions, progressing toward higher syntheses (sublation / Aufhebung) of freedom.

title: The World as Will & Metaphysical Pessimism
summary: Kant's thing-in-itself is revealed as blind, irrational Will—an eternal striving that drives all nature, producing endless suffering alleviated only through art and asceticism.

title: The Leap of Faith & Existential Dread
summary: Objective rational certainty cannot resolve religious or existential truth; the individual must make an agonizing, passionate leap into the absurd.

title: Historical Materialism & Alienation
summary: The material modes of economic production form the foundation of society; capitalism alienates workers from their labor, products, species-essence, and each other.

title: Will to Power & Revaluation of Values
summary: The fundamental cosmic and biological driving force is not mere survival, but expansion, self-overcoming, growth, and dominance.

title: The Eternal Recurrence & Amor Fati
summary: The ultimate test of life affirmation: would you will your exact life, with every joy and sorrow, to repeat infinitely in an eternal loop?

title: The Principle of Utility & Harm Principle
summary: Actions are right in proportion to promoting happiness; society may coerce an individual only to prevent harm to others.

title: Intentionality & Phenomenological Reduction (Epoché)
summary: Consciousness is always consciousness of something (intentionality); bracketing belief in the external world reveals pure structures of experience.

title: Dasein & Being-toward-Death
summary: Human beings are not detached Cartesian observers, but embedded agents already 'thrown' into a world, achieving authenticity by confronting mortality.

title: Existence Precedes Essence & Bad Faith
summary: Man first exists, encounters himself in the world, and only then defines who he is; pretending we have no freedom of choice is the cowardice of bad faith.

title: The Absurd & Sisyphus's Revolt
summary: The tension between human longing for inherent purpose and the cold indifference of the cosmos; revolt and defiance give life dignity.

title: Language Games & Forms of Life
summary: The meaning of a word is its use within a shared social practice (language game); philosophical problems arise when language 'goes on holiday'.

title: Falsificationism & Demarcation
summary: A scientific theory can never be conclusively verified by positive evidence; it is genuine science only if it makes risky predictions that could be proven false.

title: Disciplinary Power & The Panopticon
summary: Modern power is not merely top-down sovereign violence; it is diffuse, institutional, shaping our bodies and concepts through internalization of constant surveillance.

title: Deconstruction & Différance
summary: Language cannot offer unmediated access to reality; meaning is perpetually deferred and defined only through relational differences across texts.

title: The Banality of Evil
summary: Catastrophic moral atrocities are often committed not by demonic sadists, but by thoughtless conformists faithfully operating within bureaucratic systems.

title: The Veil of Ignorance & Difference Principle
summary: Fair societal rules are designed when deciders do not know their own class, race, gender, or abilities in advance, ensuring protection for the least advantaged.

title: The Burnout Society & Self-Exploitation
summary: The modern achievement subject exploits themselves under the illusion of freedom, producing psychic exhaustion, depression, and endless compulsive hyper-productivity.

title: The Simulation Argument
summary: Trilemma showing that at least one proposition is true: civilizations go extinct before technological maturity, mature civilizations don't run ancestor simulations, or we almost certainly live in a simulation.
